> It's possible to pass subtypes there in the "domainName" argument:

We need some special handling for these anyway, since we need to advertise a PTR from the selective name with subtype to the usual name without a subtype.

Looks like it works. `_http._sub._qotd._tcp.local.` was advertised by resolved and the mDNS responder on another machine saw it. The "Deregister" method deregistered the service too in the sense that goodbye packets were sent and `dns-sd` showed that:
```
dns-sd -B _qotd._tcp,_http
Browsing for _qotd._tcp,_http
DATE: ---Sat 16 Mar 2024---
 6:26:16.939  ...STARTING...
Timestamp     A/R    Flags  if Domain               Service Type         Instance Name
 6:28:09.800  Add        2  13 local.               _qotd._tcp.          H
 6:38:38.578  Rmv        0  13 local.               _qotd._tcp.          H
```

Interestingly it turns out resolved advertises all RRs with ttl=120 even though according to https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6762#section-10 some RRs should come with ttl=4500. Known-answer suppression doesn't seem to work:
```
<Ether  dst=01:00:5e:00:00:fb src=4a:d7:05:2c:1d:64 type=IPv4 |<IP  version=4 ihl=5 tos=0x0 len=89 id=12913 flags= frag=0 ttl=255 proto=udp chksum=0x0 src=192.168.56.3 dst=224.0.0.251 |<UDP  sport=mdns dport=mdns len=69 chksum=0xd9fd |<DNS  id=0 qr=0 opcode=QUERY aa=0 tc=0 rd=0 ra=0 z=0 ad=0 cd=0 rcode=ok qdcount=1 ancount=1 nscount=0 arcount=0 qd=[<DNSQR  qname=b'_http._sub._qotd._tcp.local.' qtype=PTR qclass=IN |>] an=[<DNSRR  rrname=b'_http._sub._qotd._tcp.local.' type=PTR rclass=IN ttl=115 rdata=b'H._qotd._tcp.local.' |>] |>>>>
<Ether  dst=01:00:5e:00:00:fb src=08:00:27:0b:2f:0b type=IPv4 |<IP  version=4 ihl=5 tos=0x0 len=83 id=12564 flags= frag=0 ttl=255 proto=udp chksum=0xb0dd src=192.168.56.4 dst=224.0.0.251 |<UDP  sport=mdns dport=mdns len=63 chksum=0x70a |<DNS  id=0 qr=1 opcode=QUERY aa=1 tc=0 rd=0 ra=0 z=0 ad=0 cd=0 rcode=ok qdcount=0 ancount=1 nscount=0 arcount=0 an=[<DNSRR  rrname=b'_http._sub._qotd._tcp.local.' type=PTR rclass=IN ttl=120 rdata=b'H._qotd._tcp.local.' |>] |>>>>
```
but it has nothing to do with this PR.

Looks like it violates the RFC (a bit) in the sense that `resolved` advertises RRs pointing `_services._dns-sd._udp.local` to `_http._sub._qotd._tcp.local.`:
```sh
-bash-5.2# dig @192.168.124.17 -p 5353 _services._dns-sd._udp.local ANY +notcp +noall +ans
_services._dns-sd._udp.local. 120 IN    PTR     _http._sub._qotd._tcp.local.
_services._dns-sd._udp.local. 120 IN    PTR     _qotd._tcp.local.
```
but according to https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc6763#section-9 the rdata should be two labels plus a domain:
> A DNS query for
   PTR records with the name "_services._dns-sd._udp.<Domain>" yields a
   set of PTR records, where the rdata of each PTR record is the two-
   label <Service> name, plus the same domain, e.g.,
   "_http._tcp.<Domain>".

I've just checked and `mDNSResponder` doesn't advertise RRs like that. It just adds PTR RRs pointing subtypes to service instance names.

issue_context.title: implement DNS-SD subtypes in systemd-resolved
issue_context.body:
**Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.**
The [DNS-SD RFC](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc6763#section-7.1) use subtype to represent a more detail protocol of primary protocols.
But systemd-resolved is not support the subtypes currently.

**Describe the solution you'd like**

Add a new config field named `Subtype` in `*.dnssd`. When the user specify one or more `Subtype`, systemd-resolved should response to corresponding subtype query request.
